title: The question
body: The interviewer says: "Given a list of numbers and a target, return the positions of two numbers that add up to the target." Example: [7, 2, 11, 15, 4] with target 6. Before anything else, listen and repeat the question in your own words.
code:
// 1 clarify  2 examples  3 brute force  4 improve
// 5 code  6 test  7 explain

title: Clarify
body: Ask about what the statement leaves open: Can numbers repeat? Can one number be used twice? Is there always exactly one answer? Return positions or values? Here: exactly one answer, two different positions, return the positions. Limits: up to 100,000 numbers.
code: // n ≤ 10^5 → aim for O(n) or O(n log n)

title: Brute force first
body: Say the simple idea out loud: try every pair. It is correct and shows you understand the task, but it is O(n²), about 5 × 10⁹ pairs for 100,000 numbers. Too slow, so look for something better.

title: Improve
body: Each number x needs exactly one partner: target − x. If the numbers already seen are stored in a hash map from value to position, finding the partner takes O(1). One pass gives O(n) time and O(n) space.
code: const seen = new Map();   // value → position

predict.question: Scanning left to right, what should you remember so that each number's partner can be found at once?
options: Each number seen so far and its position, in a hash map
Only the largest number so far
The sum of everything so far
predict.explanation: The partner of x is target − x. If every earlier number is in a hash map, checking for the partner is O(1).

title: Trace position 0
body: Position 0: 7 needs -1, which has not been seen. Store 7 → 0 and move on.

title: Trace position 1
body: Position 1: 2 needs 4, which has not been seen. Store 2 → 1 and move on.

title: Trace position 2
body: Position 2: 11 needs -5, which has not been seen. Store 11 → 2 and move on.

title: Trace position 3
body: Position 3: 15 needs -9, which has not been seen. Store 15 → 3 and move on.

title: Trace position 4
body: Position 4: 4 needs 2. 2 is in the map at position 1, so the answer is [1, 4]. Stop.

predict.question: Position 4 holds 4, so it needs 2. The map holds 7→0, 2→1, 11→2, 15→3. What happens?
options: 2 is in the map at 1: return [1, 4]
2 is missing: add 4 and go on

title: Test
body: Run the code on cases that could break it, out loud: [3, 3] with target 6 (the same value twice: the map check happens before storing, so it works); a pair at the very end; negative numbers; the smallest input of two numbers.

title: Explain
body: Finish with the summary an interviewer wants to hear: one pass with a hash map, O(n) time and O(n) space. Mention the trade-off: sorting with two pointers uses O(1) extra space but O(n log n) time, and loses the original positions unless you keep them.
